project.name: Re-CTM
project.target: A single installable OAuth MCP runtime combining exact CTM computer tools, a Rethlas-derived verified mathematical workflow, and a private cross-run Verified Research Workspace.

product_constraints.dangerous_scope: Native CMT computer-tool authority only; it must never bypass Rethlas workflow authorization.

architecture_decisions.decision: Ship CMT-derived runtime and Rethlas-derived methodology in one Re-CTM package.
Expose Re-CTM over HTTP MCP with OAuth only; bearer/noauth are out of product scope.
Keep native CMT safe/trusted/dangerous modes. These modes govern native computer tools only.
Implement a second, orthogonal Rethlas workflow authorization plane: OAuth identity AND run capability AND role ACL AND workflow state.
CMT dangerous authority must not imply or grant any Rethlas workflow capability.
Rethlas workflow isolation applies only while using the rethlas_* super-tool surface; native CMT tools retain their own permission semantics.
Prevent dangerous native tools from bypassing Rethlas isolation by keeping the Rethlas private run store outside the native tool trust domain, with an OS-level boundary or equivalent hard isolation.
Replace Rethlas subagents with isolated reasoning domains: frozen snapshot, branch-local read/write capability, sealed result, and explicit join. Physical execution may be sequential.
Preserve Generator, branch, join, verifier, repair, and finalize roles as workflow domains even when one web model performs the turns sequentially.
Make verifier final verdict and final artifact publication server-gated mechanical transitions, not model-controlled labels.

Retain Rethlas memory, search, examples, counterexamples, decomposition plans, direct proving, recursive branch exploration, failure synthesis, independent verifier data firewall, repair loop, and strict stopping rules.
Remove Zola/site delivery and Markdown final delivery; use proof.tex and proof_verified.tex, with a LaTeX compile gate before verification/finalization.
The web conversation is the user-facing controller; persistent workflow state must live server-side and survive browser disconnects.
Re-CTM must be a strict tool-surface superset of Coding Tools MCP: preserve all 18 CTM native tools and command lifecycle semantics, then add Rethlas tools without removing or hiding CTM tools.

Preserve CTM-class reverse-proxy OAuth convenience: RE_CTM_SERVER_URL is an optional fixed override, while an unset value enables per-request OAuth-origin derivation only on loopback-bound servers using validated Host and loopback-trusted forwarded headers. Fixed origins always win and dynamic mode is rejected on non-loopback binds. Preserve the Coding Tools MCP Origin-policy route boundary: actual OAuth metadata/registration/authorization/token routes do not inherit the MCP Origin rejection gate, while MCP transport and OPTIONS remain origin-gated. Keep the OAuth authorization page compatible with the registered external callback; unlike the earlier Re-CTM page, do not emit form-action 'self', which Chromium may apply to the post-submit 302 redirect chain.

Preserve CTM-class OAuth operator convenience: RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD is optional for interactive serve; if absent, generate a high-entropy authorization key for that serve session and reveal it only to the local operator terminal, never to structured logs, reports, HTTP responses, or persistent state.

Use MCP server instructions and the rethlas_start tool contract to route concrete mathematical proof, derivation, proof-repair, and rigorous verification requests into the Rethlas workflow by default; allow a direct chat answer only when the user explicitly requests an informal bypass.

When an MCP-driven Rethlas run reaches done, automatically export the mechanically finalized final_tex through the controlled artifact bridge to a workspace-relative path, defaulting to rethlas-output/<run_id>/proof_verified.tex. Repeated identical exports are idempotent; different existing content is never overwritten automatically.

Reduce the LLM-facing Rethlas protocol to six façade tools: rethlas_start, rethlas_step, rethlas_inspect, rethlas_retrieve, rethlas_control, and rethlas_artifact. Preserve the exact 18-tool CTM public prefix and continue accepting superseded Rethlas protocol names as hidden compatibility aliases rather than advertising them in tools/list.

Make workflow submissions LLM-oriented rather than JSON-echo-oriented: server-issued plan/subgoal ids are authoritative, direct screening may be submitted incrementally, incomplete coverage returns exact missing ids without transition, plan/outcome/branch-set fields are server-derived, and validation/conflict failures from rethlas_step keep accepted logical writes while returning a recoverable current task.

On Linux, automatically use the built-in Bubblewrap native backend when bwrap is installed and require its startup attestation to succeed. In dangerous mode, expose the host PATH plus narrowly discovered read-only user toolchain roots (including Conda/Sage prefixes and PATH symlink targets such as Magma) while continuing to exclude Re-CTM data/private roots. Manual isolation validation remains release evidence rather than a runtime enablement flag.

Supersede per-application native-tool compatibility with one Native Toolchain Exposure Policy. Build the Bubblewrap view from system roots, non-system PATH prefixes, executable-symlink target prefixes, and operator-declared RE_CTM_NATIVE_EXEC_ALLOW_ROOTS; canonicalize and ancestor-collapse the union, extend sandbox PATH for explicit bin/sbin/Executables directories, reject relative/missing/broad/workspace/data/private-overlapping roots, mount every accepted non-system root read-only, report a diagnostic plan, and revalidate protected boundaries inside the Bubblewrap command builder. No Sage, Magma, Mathematica, Maple, or other product-name branch is permitted.

Make every model-active Rethlas task a zero-guess self-describing contract. The task envelope exposes write_contract, exact commit_action, commit_payload_schema, and a schema-valid minimal/template/example submission. Do not require model writes for server-derived canonical records such as decomposition plans, failure synthesis, or replanning decisions. Strictly validate plan list fields instead of coercing strings into character arrays. Any validation/conflict correction handled by rethlas_step returns recoverable=true, retryable=true, a fresh capability, retained-write information, and guidance not to replay retained records; permission/security failures stay hard.

Make Re-CTM v0.2.0 a Verified Research Workspace rather than only a per-run proof engine. Persist private owner-scoped projects, claims, immutable claim revisions, dependency/supersession edges, project-run links, and portable project manifests. OPEN claims may be owner-created, but VERIFIED/CONDITIONAL revisions originate only from mechanically finalized correct runs; Native dangerous has no project verification authority.

Add a Compact Verified Lane without adding new workflow roles/states: protocol-2 assess may route a direct self-contained task to assemble, but compact still traverses LaTeX validation, independent verifier, repair, and finalizer. Compact assembly can escalate to full exploration and a second wrong compact verifier result automatically escalates to full explore.

Freeze project knowledge at run start and require protocol-2 proof_manifest alongside proof.tex. The manifest declares target statement, proof-used dependency revision ids, material reference ids, conditional hypotheses, and computational evidence; dependencies must come from the frozen verified project snapshot and conditions propagate mechanically through promoted revisions.

Replace the earlier references:approved alias semantics with explicit reference provenance and per-proof verifier audit. Inline/retrieved references receive stable ids and source snapshots/hashes; every material proof reference needs a SOURCE_VERIFIED, INDEPENDENTLY_REDERIVED, UNRESOLVED, or NOT_MATERIAL disposition, and unresolved/missing coverage is mechanically inserted into verification gaps before verdict computation.

Extend the existing rethlas_retrieve façade with typed theorem_search, paper_search, paper_lookup, and theorem_context operations. Keep theorem search bounded and use a fixed validated HTTPS bibliographic provider for paper operations; never accept an arbitrary caller-supplied URL fetch target or treat retrieved material as verified by default.

Version the persistent StateStore schema and workflow protocol independently. Migrate supported older SQLite schemas additively with recorded migration history, fail closed on newer unsupported schemas, create new MCP runs with workflow protocol 2, and let persisted protocol-1 runs continue with their original contracts after upgrade.

Add native command termination provenance as diagnostics only. Report requested timeout, elapsed time, observed signal, and whether Re-CTM sent TERM/KILL, classifying unmatched signals as external_or_unknown; do not change the original CTM command timeout/TERM/KILL lifecycle in v0.2.0.

Keep the public catalog exactly 24 tools in v0.2.0: the exact 18 CTM prefix plus the same six Rethlas façade tools. Add project, compact, provenance, retrieval, and artifact capabilities through typed additive arguments/operations rather than multiplying public protocol tools.

L2.name: Rethlas workflow authority
L2.purpose: Authorize private reasoning resources and workflow transitions.

L2P.name: Research project authority
L2P.purpose: Authorize owner-scoped project/claim inspection and OPEN-claim administration. It never grants mechanical verification/finalization authority.

authorization_model.rethlas_tool_rule: allow = L0 AND run_capability AND role_acl AND workflow_state
authorization_model.project_verified_promotion_rule: allow_verified_promotion = mechanically_finalized_correct_run AND project_link AND optimistic_base_match; never model/native controlled
authorization_model.non_inheritance_axiom: L1 dangerous does not imply any L2 capability.
authorization_model.private_store_rule: Rethlas private state must not be directly readable through native CMT tools, including dangerous mode.

branch_semantics.visibility: self branch plus snapshot only until join
branch_semantics.join: other branch results become visible only after all required branches are sealed

engineering_debug_notes.symptom: Two large apply_patch envelopes were rejected as ambiguous or because they attempted delete-and-add of the same path in one envelope.
engineering_debug_notes.resolution: Split changes into narrow atomic patches; rejected envelopes did not modify source files.
engineering_debug_notes.preventive_action: Use small exact-context patches for security-sensitive routing code and verify immediately after each patch.

engineering_debug_notes.symptom: Initial Git identity was absent, so the repository could not be committed without choosing an author.
engineering_debug_notes.resolution: Confirmed Peter Liu and the numeric GitHub noreply address from public I0amLK commits, then configured them only in Re-CTM/.git/config.
engineering_debug_notes.preventive_action: Never infer or expose a private email; prefer an identity already present in public commits and record its provenance.

engineering_debug_notes.symptom: The non-interactive HTTPS push failed before authentication because the runtime has no GitHub credential helper, token, or interactive username prompt; SSH port 22 was also unavailable.
engineering_debug_notes.resolution: Preserved both local commits, kept origin configured, and recorded the exact blocker without embedding credentials in the repository.
engineering_debug_notes.preventive_action: Push from an authenticated shell or install a credential helper; never place a personal access token in a remote URL, environment example, debug bundle, or project ledger.

engineering_debug_notes.symptom: At the original deployment checkpoint, the standalone OAuth/MCP smoke used RE_CTM_OAUTH_SERVER_URL and RE_CTM_PORT, while that version still required RE_CTM_SERVER_URL and the CLI initially ignored RE_CTM_PORT. A busy default port then exposed a bind-failure cleanup AttributeError.
engineering_debug_notes.scope: deployment configuration and HTTP server construction
engineering_debug_notes.resolution: Corrected deployment documentation, made serve defaults honor RE_CTM_HOST/RE_CTM_PORT, assigned the application before ThreadingHTTPServer binds, added a bind-failure regression, and reran the full redacted smoke successfully. AD-015 later removed the loopback/Quick-Tunnel requirement for RE_CTM_SERVER_URL while retaining it as the fixed-origin override.
engineering_debug_notes.preventive_action: Keep config.example.env, deployment docs, CLI defaults, and standalone smoke under the same regression suite; preserve original OS errors on partial construction failure.

known_risks.risk: A native dangerous tool could bypass branch/verifier isolation if Rethlas private state is visible in the same OS trust domain.
known_risks.mitigation: Use a hard OS-level boundary or equivalent isolation so native tools cannot directly access the private store.

known_risks.risk: One web model executing domains sequentially does not provide perfect cognitive amnesia between branches.
known_risks.mitigation: Enforce frozen inputs, resource ACLs, sealed branch outputs, materially different branch strategies, and strict verifier audit stages.

known_risks.risk: MCP clients may cache tool catalogs or annotations.
known_risks.mitigation: Keep a stable tool catalog; enforce role/state authorization server-side instead of dynamically hiding tools.

known_risks.risk: The word dangerous may be mistakenly interpreted as bypassing mathematical correctness gates.
known_risks.mitigation: Specify and test the non-inheritance axiom: native dangerous never grants workflow or finalization authority.

known_risks.risk: The packaged Linux bubblewrap helper is still an operational articulation point whose guarantees depend on the target kernel, bubblewrap packaging, mount layout, and operator configuration.
known_risks.mitigation: The built-in Bubblewrap backend performs mandatory fail-closed attestation on every startup; manual_native_isolation_test.py remains release/target evidence rather than a runtime acknowledgement gate. External helpers still require explicit operator attestation.

known_risks.risk: Loopback OAuth and MCP tests may not match the final webpage host's protocol and redirect behavior.
known_risks.mitigation: Retain dual-era MCP handling, mirror-header validation, fixed catalog, locally test Cloudflare-style dynamic issuer/resource binding, and execute MV-001/MV-002 on the real host after push.

known_risks.risk: A successful isolated compile on the reference host is not equivalent to compilation on every target TeX distribution.
known_risks.mitigation: Production defaults to latex_policy=required, compilation never falls back to the host namespace, and MV-007 must be completed with each target latexmk/TeX Live distribution.

known_risks.risk: The theorem-search service may return irrelevant, incorrectly matched, context-dependent, or unavailable external statements.
known_risks.mitigation: Bound response size and HTTPS endpoint configuration, mark every result external_unverified, persist provenance identifiers, require source-context/definition/applicability checks, and keep web/manual fallback in the methodology.

known_risks.risk: The built-in bubblewrap backend supports the full CTM command_id lifecycle, while arbitrary third-party external helper protocols may only implement synchronous execution unless extended with an equivalent lifecycle transport.
known_risks.mitigation: Treat bubblewrap as the reference Linux compatibility backend, expose lifecycle support in check_exec_environment, fail clearly for unsupported helper behavior, and complete MV-009 on every supported deployment backend.

known_risks.risk: Reflecting untrusted forwarding headers into OAuth issuer/resource values could let a public request influence authorization authority.
known_risks.mitigation: Explicit RE_CTM_SERVER_URL always wins; otherwise dynamic origin mode is accepted only on a loopback-bound server, forwarded headers are trusted only from a loopback peer, Host is strictly validated, tokens remain issuer/audience-bound to the effective origin, and non-loopback dynamic bind is rejected. Origin validation remains a separate transport defense and follows the Coding Tools MCP boundary: MCP/OPTIONS are gated without applying that gate globally to OAuth endpoints.

known_risks.risk: Automatically generated OAuth authorization keys improve tunnel usability but become sensitive local-terminal material that could leak if copied into structured diagnostics or persistent state.
known_risks.mitigation: Generate the key only for interactive serve, reveal it only after successful HTTP bind to the local operator terminal, keep check-config secret-free, never include the raw key in structured debug/state/report payloads, and cover the behavior with INV-010/MV-001.

known_risks.risk: MCP server instructions and tool descriptions strongly influence mathematical task routing but a particular webpage host may ignore or truncate them and answer directly instead of starting Rethlas.
known_risks.mitigation: Make the routing rule explicit in both initialize instructions and rethlas_start metadata, keep an ordinary-language real-client test in MV-008, report this host limitation honestly, and retain explicit user wording as a fallback rather than pretending server-side prompt interception exists.

known_risks.risk: rethlas_step may successfully append logical memory records before a later commit-format validation fails, so a naive client retry could duplicate non-screening memory records.
known_risks.mitigation: Treat validation/conflict failures as recoverable submissions rather than tool errors, explicitly return writes_retained and a fresh current task/capability, revoke the capability used for the superseded step, keep direct-screening progress id-keyed and overwrite-idempotent, and require real-client MV-008 evidence that the host follows the returned correction instead of replaying retained writes.

known_risks.risk: PATH discovery cannot infer every hidden runtime/library/database directory of arbitrarily packaged scientific software, while overly broad roots could expose unrelated host data.
known_risks.mitigation: Use application-agnostic prefix and symlink discovery for the common case, RE_CTM_NATIVE_EXEC_ALLOW_ROOTS for operator-declared split installations, one canonical overlap gate for every source, strict existence/absolute/broad-root checks, ancestor collapse, read-only mounts, helper-side revalidation, diagnostic plans, and MV-003 target evidence.

Strengthened Rethlas workflow contracts: complete direct screening, exact one-branch-per-plan rounds, all-branch joins, branch evidence requirements, verifier audit prerequisites, persisted verification reports, and changed-proof repair.

Added capability-gated theorem retrieval, live endpoint smoke, Apache-2.0 attribution, GitHub Actions CI, 26 passing tests, clean wheel installation, and installed helper attestation. Full post-push manual acceptance remains at zero percent.

Created checkpoint commit 106959b7a0407ee3a69156d1d111f93c2d8a61dc, configured origin to https://github.com/I0amLK/Re-CTM.git, and attempted non-interactive HTTPS/SSH push. Push is blocked by missing runtime credentials/SSH transport, not by repository state.

Implemented rethlas_export_final as the sole mechanically-finalized private-to-native artifact bridge, added workspace confinement and overwrite baselines, moved graph vertex V28 to implemented_local, and retained the fixed catalog at 19 tools.

Added target deployment guidance and a credential-redacted OAuth/MCP smoke. Fixed environment-driven serve host/port defaults and bind-failure cleanup; the standalone smoke passed DCR, PKCE, token exchange, legacy MCP, 19-tool catalog, modern mirror headers, and dangerous non-inheritance.
Added CLI environment-default regressions and reran the deterministic suite at 30 passing tests; local-validation.json remains green while manual-validation.json remains pending_post_push.

Built both sdist and wheel, installed the wheel in a clean environment, passed installed helper attestation, started the installed service from RE_CTM_HOST/RE_CTM_PORT, and passed the redacted OAuth/MCP smoke against that installed service.

Rewrote README.md as an end-user usage guide covering installation from GitHub, directory preparation, OAuth configuration, web MCP connection, native modes, isolated exec enablement, Rethlas runs, progress/steering/resume/cancel, theorem retrieval, proof_verified.tex export, LaTeX policy, smoke testing, and debugging without exposing implementation internals.

Promoted CTM compatibility to a hard non-regression contract: restored all 18 CTM native tool definitions exactly (including input/output schemas and annotations), patch envelopes, Git/image/environment/permission tools, server-side argument validation, and bubblewrap command_id lifecycle with TTY stdin, retained-output paging, polling, timeout, and termination. The fixed catalog is now 31 tools and 38 local tests pass; MV-009 tracks target CTM parity.

Restored reverse-proxy OAuth convenience for Cloudflare Quick Tunnel: RE_CTM_SERVER_URL is optional on loopback binds, the effective OAuth origin is derived per request from validated Host and loopback-trusted forwarding headers, fixed origins remain authoritative, authorization-code/token issuer and audience binding follows the effective origin, non-loopback dynamic bind is denied, the package version advances to 0.1.0.dev1 for unambiguous upgrades, and the deterministic suite now contains 42 passing tests.

Restored CTM-style OAuth operator-key convenience: interactive serve now auto-generates a 32-byte-url-safe authorization key when RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD is absent, reveals it only after a successful local bind, check-config reports generated_on_serve without materializing the key, a runtime probe confirmed a 43-character generated key with no structured-state leak, and the deterministic suite now contains 43 passing tests.

Corrected Re-CTM's over-broad browser Origin gate after comparing the Coding Tools MCP reference implementation and compliance tests: actual OAuth metadata/registration/authorization/token routes no longer inherit MCP Origin rejection, while /mcp and OPTIONS remain origin-gated. Added regressions for an Origin-bearing Quick Tunnel authorization POST and preserved denial of unapproved MCP/OPTIONS origins; the deterministic suite now contains 44 passing tests.

Compared the OAuth authorization HTML response with Coding Tools MCP after observing successful /oauth/authorize 302 responses with no subsequent /oauth/token request. Removed Re-CTM's extra Content-Security-Policy form-action 'self' header, which can block a form-submission redirect to the registered ChatGPT callback in Chromium, and added a regression that the authorization response no longer carries that CSP. The OAuth code/token protocol itself was left unchanged.

Strengthened the MCP mathematical-routing contract so concrete proof/derivation/repair/verification requests default to rethlas_start, added an optional workspace export_path to run creation, and made terminal rethlas_next automatically create the mechanically verified proof_verified.tex under rethlas-output/<run_id>/ by default. Automatic export is idempotent for identical bytes and refuses to overwrite different content; the explicit alternate export tool remains available.

Refactored the LLM-facing Rethlas protocol from 13 advertised low-level tools to six façade tools while retaining eleven superseded names as hidden call-compatible aliases. rethlas_step now combines logical writes, commit, and advancement; validation/conflict corrections are recoverable with retained-write disclosure. Direct screening now uses server-issued plan/subgoal ids, accepts incremental coverage, derives plan status/outcome/branch sets server-side, and branch join derives sealed-branch coverage/outcome. The deterministic suite contains 48 passing tests and a clean installed dev3 OAuth/MCP smoke confirms 24 public tools plus hidden-alias compatibility.

Restored meaningful Native dangerous execution without weakening the Rethlas vault boundary. Linux installs now auto-select built-in Bubblewrap when available and perform mandatory startup attestation without requiring RE_CTM_NATIVE_ISOLATION_ATTESTED=1. Dangerous-mode execution inherits the host PATH plus narrowly discovered read-only user toolchain roots while excluding configured data/private roots. On the reference target, source and clean-wheel dev4 runtimes both executed SageMath, Magma, and ordinary shell commands successfully; the deterministic suite now contains 50 passing tests.

Replaced software-by-software compatibility with a generic Native Toolchain Exposure Policy. Added RE_CTM_NATIVE_EXEC_ALLOW_ROOTS, canonical system/PATH/symlink/explicit union planning, filtered inherited PATH, common bin/sbin/Executables PATH extension, broad/missing/relative/trust-domain overlap denials, ancestor collapse, read-only Bubblewrap mounts, helper-protocol propagation and revalidation, startup mount-plan probing, diagnostics, target manual probes, INV-011/PC-013/AD-022, 62 passing tests, and a clean dev5 wheel smoke covering an arbitrary explicit toolchain plus SageMath, Magma, shell, and mutation denial.

Converted every model-active Rethlas task into a zero-guess self-describing contract after two live workflow exercises exposed hidden JSON assumptions. Added exact write_contract and commit_payload_schema data, schema-valid submissions/templates, server-derived-record non-duplication for planning/failure/replan, strict plan-array typing with dependency preservation, write-time as well as commit-time recoverable corrections with retryable/fresh-capability/retained-write guidance, hard permission-error preservation, startup methodology-contract validation, a no-schema-correction end-to-end façade regression through automatic proof_verified.tex export, 70 passing deterministic tests, PC-014/AD-023/MV-008 acceptance criteria, and a clean dev6 wheel smoke confirming the packaged contracts and 24-tool catalog.
